title: Practical and Ethical Challenges of Large Language Models in Education: A Systematic Scoping Review

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic scoping review and thematic analysis of 118 peer-reviewed papers to quantify the distribution of languages supported by LLM-based educational innovations, highlighting the dominance of English-centric models and potential biases against non-native English speakers.

Reviewing the literature to evaluate the frequency with which educational LLM studies report descriptive demographic data of sample groups (such as gender and ethnicity) and whether they address algorithmic fairness and systematic discrimination.

Assessing the included literature for ethical considerations regarding equal access to LLM innovations, specifically analyzing mentions of limitations for students from low-income backgrounds, rural areas, and non-WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) societies.
